reviewScope: Black Whale vessel, spatial, access, operational, structural and scale evidence only

pass1.method: Full-page visual sweep of all 19 ordered pages

pass2.method: Full-resolution verification of communal areas, tier schematic, warehouse spaces, service passages, cargo storage and access-control evidence

retainedPanels.subject: Five-tier schematic
retainedPanels.visualDescription: An in-story schematic depicts the five-tier hierarchy and population grouping.
modelingProhibitions: Do not convert the schematic into measured geometry

retainedPanels.subject: Tall industrial warehouse
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A tall plain compartment contains stacked crates, structural bays and open work floor.

retainedPanels.subject: Cargo-filled storage compartment
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A broad storage room contains stacked cargo and multiple people with open aisles.
modelingPermissions: Represent cargo aisles and storage density
modelingProhibitions: Do not count unseen crates or bays

retainedPanels.subject: Restricted-entry sign
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A prominent sign marks a prohibited-entry boundary in a crowded lower-tier area.
modelingProhibitions: Do not infer the full jurisdiction of the restriction

evidence.claim: A densely occupied communal area contains tables and food service.
A richly furnished room supports seating, attendants and service furniture.
A broad hall contains dense rows of occupants.
A formal room supports standing groups and decorative surfaces.
A schematic depicts the five-tier hierarchy and population distribution.
A tall plain compartment contains stacked crates, structural bays and open work floor.
A narrow industrial passage connects occupied lower-tier spaces.
A broad storage compartment contains stacked cargo and multiple people.
A transition occurs between industrial spaces using a nonstandard route effect.
A prominent sign marks a prohibited-entry boundary in a crowded lower-tier area.
A heavy plain threshold and wall structure frame a lower-tier access point.
Human figures and stacked crates establish a high-ceiling industrial volume.
Open circulation aisles remain between cargo stacks and occupied work areas.
Access restriction operates within an actively occupied public lower-tier area.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Tier diagram
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: The in-story tier diagram is a schematic hierarchy, not production geometry.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Teleport-route effects
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: Nen transition effects establish operational route use but not physical corridor continuity.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Restricted-entry signage
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: The sign confirms access control; its jurisdiction and exact boundary remain uncertain.

unresolvedQuestions: Which physical routes correspond to the tier schematic?
Where does the nonstandard route begin and end?
What authority controls the restricted area?

excludedMaterial.reason: Excluded pages do not independently establish ship evidence.
